about: Concept map data. Each node has two versions: the illyria field is the Original Text Illyria and the keys field is Our Illyria. I kept the field names so I don't have to rewrite the code that reads them; only the labels on the page changed. basis: notes = from the team's concept-map notes; stated = a production decision stated in conversation; draft = a first guess to confirm. An edge label reads as a sentence: [a] [label] [b]. Change any text here.

illyria.label: Viola / Cesario
illyria.note: Shipwrecked, believes her brother drowned, and takes service with Orsino disguised as a young man. She falls for Orsino while wooing Olivia for him.

keys.label: Viola / Cesario
keys.note: In the storm, Viola is buoyed by a piece of Sebastian's luggage. Viola's gender expression may have been more femme in their past life, but finding themself in a foreign place where they can explore their gender more freely (and given the contents of Sebastian's luggage as their only resource), this becomes an opportunity for them to work through grief, carve out a new life for themself, and explore being perceived in a different way by the world. Since our Illyria is a queer-er world, adopting masculine attire is more about opportunity and intrigue than it is about protection.

context.t: Boys and young men played all the female roles, so Viola was a boy playing a woman who disguises herself as a boy.
The cross-dressed heroine who provokes female desire is an Italian theatre motif; English playwrights keep it but tone down the charge of it.

illyria.label: Sebastian
illyria.note: Viola's twin, also shipwrecked and thought drowned. Mistaken for Cesario, he is claimed by Olivia and marries her.

keys.label: Sebastian
keys.note: Viola's twin. Rescued from the shipwreck and nursed back to health by Antonio. After saving him from drowning, Antonio delivered him to a hospital where he remained in a coma for a month or more. Antonio visited this "John Doe" religiously (perhaps giving him the name Rodrigo). After he regained consciousness, Antonio stood by him for another month through his rehabilitation and the aftermath of the amnesia from the traumatic brain injury suffered in the shipwreck. During this time, a romantic relationship blossomed. When we meet these two at the top of Act 2, Sebastian's memory of his sister and previous life has begun to return, and he is pulling away from Antonio in his newly-realized grief. He sees Olivia's proposal as an instantaneous class-climbing opportunity, but she's attractive to him as well. In OUR play's conclusion, Olivia is delighted that Sebastian and Antonio are a package deal, rather than Antonio having no resolution and Sebastian sailing off into heteronormative bliss.

illyria.label: Antonio
illyria.note: A sea captain who rescued Sebastian and follows him into Orsino's territory at risk of arrest. He is arrested after mistaking Viola for Sebastian.

keys.label: Antonio
keys.note: The captain of a small fishing boat, who is wanted in Illyria because of smuggling refugees and drugs onto the island. He may have also had a romantic relationship with Orsino in the past, and left him scorned, so Illyria is an unsafe place for him in general. He fell in love with Sebastian over the course of his recovery from the shipwreck, and wants to keep him safe, even if that means risking his own safety.

context.t: The early Keys economy was built on fishing, turtling, sponging, and wrecking.

illyria.label: Orsino
illyria.note: Duke of Illyria, lovesick and fond of his own sorrow. He sends Cesario to woo Olivia and ends the play claiming Viola.

keys.label: Orsino
keys.note: A new-money transplant who made his fortune in the tech world. He has come to this area to escape Silicon Valley, seeking tranquility and love. He owns and manages the resort in name only, and his staff pretty much runs the hotel of their own accord while he occupies one of the more luxurious units, indulging in self-care and pining for Olivia. In the past, he may have had a brief tryst with Antonio, and wanted to tame his wanderlust and unlawful activities. When Antonio refused to be pinned down, Orsino banned him from the property and took out restraining orders. He is taken with Cesario and may have a bigger reaction to Cesario's perceived betrayal, having grown closer to him and accustomed to Olivia's repeated rejections. Characters adjacent to Orsino include his assistants, Curio and Valentine, and his security guards (Officers).

context.t: Renaissance melancholy: lethargic, drawn to music and poetry, fond of his own sorrow as proof of the depth of his feeling.

illyria.label: Olivia
illyria.note: A countess mourning her brother for seven years (the drama). She opens up to Cesario, falls in love, and marries Sebastian by mistake.

keys.label: Olivia
keys.note: Olivia is the heiress of a large family fortune. Her family resided in the northeast, and were snowbirds who own the Penthouse suite at the Hotel Illyria as a winter retreat. Some of Olivia's fondest memories of her upbringing and life with her older brother (now deceased) happened at this resort and on these beaches. She has come here in the wake of her brother's passing to grieve and sort out her family's affairs, but is bombarded by suitors who are more interested in her as a rung on the class-climbing ladder than in her mind or spirit. She is attracted to anyone who sees beyond her fortune, and she knows her worth comprehensively. Olivia is intrigued by the gender duality inherent in Cesario, delighted when there are two of him, and open to inviting Antonio into her union with Sebastian at the play's conclusion. Olivia's desire to marry a eunuch, followed by a new opportunity to remain an enthusiastic fruit-fly to Antonio/Sebastian's union presumes that she may wish to avoid such entanglements in favor of her own autonomy. Her shrewdness in choosing a mate is observed by Sir Toby.

context.t: Conch: long-term inhabitants of Key West, usually with Bahamian and Caribbean lineage dating back to the nineteenth century.

illyria.label: Malvolio
illyria.note: Olivia's steward, called "a kind of Puritan," who imagines himself as Olivia's husband and ruler. He follows the forged letter, is treated as mad, and exits vowing revenge.

keys.label: Malvolio
keys.note: The family lawyer, and the executor of Olivia's brother's will. Obsessed with law and order, and envisions a future for himself as Olivia's lover (which comes with it belonging to the aristocracy, and a life where he won't have to practice law). He has probably had to get Sir Toby off the hook for disorderly conduct or public drunkenness on more than one occasion. He is a buzzkill, a naysayer, and an uber-conservative curmudgeon with a superiority complex. His regular clothing is restrictive and not well-suited to the tropical climate. The letter provokes him to dress in a kinky and provocative way that defies his own style and moral compass. In our interpretation, he's set up by Maria/Toby/Andrew/Fabian/Feste because he was a party pooper; they torment him relentlessly because he has sold himself out completely in pursuit of Olivia's affection/attention.

context.t: He imagines himself in various ways as Olivia's husband, and therefore her ruler or better.
Sumptuary laws restricted fabrics, colors, and styles to rank and gender, which is part of why his clothes matter.
Mobility of desire, Malvolio's or anyone's, is largely determined and controlled by the upper classes.
Military personnel and families, mostly connected to Naval Air Station, are one of Key West's community groups.

illyria.label: Maria
illyria.note: Olivia's gentlewoman. She forges the letter to take revenge on Malvolio, and marries Sir Toby.

keys.label: Maria
keys.note: Olivia's personal assistant accompanying her on a trip to the family's penthouse. Excellent at her job, but gradually prioritized revelry and revenge. She climbs the ladder from servant-class by marrying Toby (her partner in debauchery). She comes from a lower/middle class background, and is not necessarily a local of this area.

context.t: Sir Toby's Lady of Misrule: with him, a strong candidate for the play's festive ringleader.
In early modern London, women of lower status, often servants, sometimes married their masters, which allowed social mobility through marriage.

illyria.label: Feste
illyria.note: Olivia's fool, who is permitted to say what he will. He sings, trades words and witticisms with everyone, and plays Sir Topas to help in the plot to put Malvolio in his place.

keys.label: Feste
keys.note: An entertainer who moves between rich households, festival locations, and bars in the area. He's a working performer who makes a living through making art, entertaining people, and sheer charisma - part busker, part virtuoso, part karaoke host. He's able to interact with autonomy with members of every class. He's the only person on the island that can and does say what he likes when he wants to, and he's so clever and lovable that no one ever truly minds. Perhaps he is unhoused and relies on the kindness of wealthy patrons and tips from tourists to get by.

context.t: An allowed fool, generally considered the Lord of Misrule because he is the only person allowed to criticize his superiors without endangering his position or life.
But he is always allowed this freedom within the confines of his job.

illyria.label: Sir Toby Belch
illyria.note: Olivia's uncle, a drinker who runs the nightly revels (the Lord of Misrule?), keeps Sir Andrew around as a suitor and a source of money, and enjoys the plot against Malvolio.

keys.label: Sir Toby
keys.note: Olivia's uncle, who loved the party life around the family's winter home so much that he moved here and resides here full time, albeit in a much lamer bachelor's unit that he can afford on the allowance he's allotted from the family. A trust fund baby turned middle-aged New Conch. If the Lord and Lady of Misrule parallels the King and Queen of Fantasy Fest, he's probably the guy. He's an asshole, and a drunkard, but occasionally he uses it to rile up people for a good cause.

context.t: Another candidate for the Lord of Misrule: he orchestrates the foolishness, revelry, and mischief around him.

illyria.label: Sir Andrew Aguecheek
illyria.note: A foolish knight and suitor with money. Toby calls it "three thousand ducats a year." Talked into a duel with Cesario.

keys.label: Sir Andrew
keys.note: The richest, and most gullible, of Toby's friends. They both sailed through an Ivy League education on the checkbooks of their families and likely met on a dirty sofa at a frat party. One drunken night, long ago, Toby may have led Andrew to believe that they could be more than just friends, but later denied everything and tried to redirect his affections to Olivia.

context.t: Tourists sustain the island's economy; many lower-income people work multiple jobs in tourism during the season.

illyria.label: Fabian
illyria.note: A member of Olivia's household who, perhaps in boredom or spite or some combination, joins the plot against Malvolio.

keys.label: Fabian
keys.note: The poolside bartender at the Hotel Illyria. She sees a lot, people tell her a lot, she collects what she needs to stir the pot and keep her days entertaining. She is a local, who bartends at a variety of venues, and although Olivia and her entourage have always tipped her handsomely, Malvolio only ever orders water and weirds out her other regular customers, driving them to spend their money elsewhere. Toby tips her well, and they likely regularly party together after hours.

illyria.label: The shipwreck
illyria.note: Viola is washed ashore in Illyria and learns that her brother may have drowned.

keys.label: The shipwreck
keys.note: Shipwrecks are common in the Keys, and the early economy of the region was built on scavenging and profiting from wrecked materials and goods.

context.t: Wrecking, retrieving valuable items from shipwrecks, was part of the early Keys economy.

illyria.label: Cesario is sent to woo Olivia
illyria.note: Orsino takes a quick liking to Cesario and, trusting him and his youth, sends him to continue his quest to obtain Olivia's hand. Viola would like to work for Olivia at first, and later just wants to marry Orsino, and is stuck between them instead.

keys.label: Cesario is sent to woo Olivia
keys.note: The new-money businessman Orsino sends his latest confidant (cough, employee, cough) to Olivia (who is old money and doesn't have time or energy to deal with Orsino's foolishness), who is frankly sick of hearing about Orsino's empty "love" for her. This triangle is at the heart of the play's themes of both class and queer desire.

illyria.label: Olivia's seven-year mourning
illyria.note: Olivia veils herself and closes her house to suitors.

keys.label: Olivia's seven-year mourning
keys.note: Olivia's family have been wealthy snowbirds, visiting their penthouse at the Hotel Illyria for warm winters for many years. She cloisters herself in the family vacation suite, venturing out on rare occasion to bask in the sun, take a solitary walk down the resort's private beach, or reflect on her grief poolside.

illyria.label: Late Nights
illyria.note: Toby, Andrew, and Feste carouse. Malvolio scolds them. Maria sets out to take revenge on him for being a killjoy and a narc (2.3, line 105).

keys.label: Late Nights
keys.note: Fantasy Fest is an inspiration for the revelry in our FL Keys-Inspired world. In both Twelfth Night festivities and Fantasy Fest, players experience a time of revelry during which usual social rules and norms go unobserved and free joy, partying, and fun take over. Misrule is the purpose of this play and our new setting, a loosening of the rules, an embrace of chaos, a collapse of class hierarchies. The big question here is - who is allowed to keep enjoying this period of misrule and continue their fun in the Keys after "order" is restored at the end of the play?

context.t: The Lord of Misrule orchestrates the revels so class conventions collapse and everyone can party together; servants and masters may even swap roles for a while.

illyria.label: The Letter
illyria.note: Maria forges Olivia's handwriting. Malvolio finds the letter and reads it as a promise of love and greatness (2.5, line 134).

keys.label: The Letter
keys.note: Since Malvolio is a stand-in for puritanism at the time, we need to be sure we dislike him throughout the show - any performance he puts on to be what he thinks Olivia wants should not feel earnest, should always feel like he's forcing a persona for manipulation reasons.

context.t: "Some are born great, some achieve greatness, and some have greatness thrust upon 'em."

illyria.label: Yellow stockings and cross-gartering
illyria.note: Malvolio follows the letter and makes a fool of himself. Olivia grows ill of him. He is treated as though he were mad. Again, Malvolio is a stand-in for both lower class individuals who want to rise in power AND for the puritans, with whom the Catholic rulers at the time were in such conflict that the puritans eventually went off to "find" and "claim" America. Yikes!

keys.label: Yellow stockings and cross-gartering
keys.note: Malvolio, crucially, does not like what we put him in. His leather daddy cross-gartering is a giant reach into poser-dom. He is not a fan, and it is not an act of self expression. He is doing this so that he might have a better chance with Olivia. We should strongly dislike him for being hypocritical and donning attire that he would absolutely have judged others for wearing, and for representing a culture to which he would never assimilate if not for the promise of both love and status.

context.t: Sumptuary laws restricted certain fabrics, colors, and styles of clothing to rank and gender.

illyria.label: The duel
illyria.note:
In order to keep their gravy train going (i.e. exploiting Andrew for his money), Toby and Fabian convince Andrew that he needs to challenge Cesario in order to "keep" Olivia's favour (which he in fact never had in the first place). They then convince both Andrew and Cesario that the other is a great fighter, presumably just for kicks.

Antonio, out of loyalty and love for Sebastian, steps in to keep him from getting hurt and is subsequently arrested.

keys.label: The duel
keys.note:
Andrew (a weak but sweet old friend of Toby's from their college years visiting the keys for a promised vacation and an implied opportunity to hook up with his friend's hot niece, who is around their age) and Cesario (a newcomer just trying to figure out their place in this very strange, charged town) are conned into fighting for Toby and Fabian's amusement. They are both not super into fighting for their own reasons, and their fight is going to be silly.

Antonio is a working class man who sees his newcomer friend (Sebastian, mistakenly) is about to get hit by this stranger and steps into the "bar fight" to try to make sure no one gets seriously injured. Of course, being of a lower class status, the authorities assume Antonio instigated the fight and arrest him.

illyria.label: The Ending
illyria.note: The twins are reunited with some suspicion. Malvolio is laughed out of the room and vows revenge, which presumably he gets by...sailing to America and helping to colonize it? Jokes on the British monarchy, I guess... Viola returns to womanhood to secure a marriage with Orsino, who remains confused - his literally last lines while asking her to marry him are "Cesario, come, for so you shall be while you are a man".

keys.label: The Ending
keys.note: All of this, but Viola stays as they are, having learned about themselves. Orsino thinks this is a whole vibe. :) Sebastian, Antonio, and Olivia are enjoying a new life together, and Olivia has her autonomy. Our audiences walk away with the understanding that we can embrace ourselves if we are authentic to ourselves, and we will be rewarded (Viola/Cesario, Sebastian, Olivia, Orsino, Antonio, Maria, Toby) and that if we try to be someone we're not for gain, we will be punished via social ostracization (Malvolio).

context.t: Orsino keeps using Cesario, the name from when he believed Viola a man, which can imply attraction to that side of her.
At the end of the play, misrule and romance give way to the everyday world and Malvolio swears revenge. The usual rules and status return.

illyria.label: Class and Status
illyria.note: Social standing in Elizabethan England could shift with land ownership, money, profession, family background, and official state recognition. Malvolio and Maria both make attempts to climb that ladder, so to speak, and only one is successful because she does it by being herself, while he tries to change himself.

keys.label: Class and Status
keys.note: There are sort of two disparate lives in Key West. The wealthy on the island like transplants, second homeowners, old families who are set up on the island, and vacationers and tourists enjoy the perception of the area as a place where rules don't always apply and festival politics reign. Local working-class people who staff all those tourist spaces tend to struggle, and there is a high cost of living and natural stress and barriers to living in the area.

context.t: Most people were lower class, 90 to 95 percent of the population, according to Lawrence Stone.
About 44% of Key West households are below the ALICE threshold (Asset Limited, Income Constrained, Employed).

illyria.label: Grief and melancholy
illyria.note: In the Renaissance, melancholy is an illness, an imbalance of bodily fluids or "humours" that is honestly kind of hot in a tortured-artist-genius way. Orsino is performing melancholy, in love with his sorrow and how he thinks it makes him look to others. Olivia is exaggerating her mourning for similar reasons, though she also has a melancholy that is rooted in legitimate grief. Both of them, frankly, have too much time and money on their hands.

keys.label: Grief and melancholy
keys.note:
In our modern setting, we understand melancholy as at most a mental health situation, and generally as a generic feeling of woe. We may rib our friends gently for being as dramatic about a girl they don't even know as Orsino is for Olivia. Orsino perhaps sees Olivia's status as a perk of dating/marrying her, and thinks they'd be the perfect "power couple". Olivia is annoyed by this, and keeps shooting him down but he just isn't getting the message.

Olivia's grief takes on new context in the modern time as well, and her performance of grief (7 years of observance) reads as extremely dramatic now, in many ways, as does her exaggerated performance of mourning. So much of comedy and camp comes from a place of pain and grief, and the circumstances of this play have their roots in fresh grief from recently departed siblings. This is a bigger conversation, and will be a major driver in our exploration of this material.

illyria.label: Marriage and money
illyria.note:
Marriage in Elizabethan England in the upper classes was tied to family expectation, social standing, and political and economic interests. It is truly a contract, and in the true royalty there may have still been arranged marriages as early as the individual's birth. Olivia and Orsino, and for that matter the somewhat lower Viola and Sebastian, would have had more options, but the implications of marrying Orsino for Olivia would be a lessening of her freedom and a transfer of her money, and in the opposite direction, Orsino would improve his reputation and gain much from the advantageous coupling.

Marrying "up", as a lower/working class person like Malvolio or Maria would have been unlikely, and if at all would be possible only for Maria and not for Malvolio due to gender dynamics. The way they both act in this play is meant to reflect the politics of the festival period of Twelfth Night, when disruption of the regular social order is encouraged and chaos reigns for the period of revelry.

keys.label: Marriage and money
keys.note:
We have a much less restricted view of marriage now, and people semi-regularly marry across class lines and in a variety of gender configurations as numerous as the gender spectrum is. Marriage is also no longer the only recognized way to be legally and socially protected as a couple, which provides us a way into the Sebastian-Olivia-Antonio situation that is alternative to the original text's solution.

Despite the potential for "upward mobility" through marriage, class-diverse marriages would still be a little strange for those in the upper class and may impact their social status, reputation, or financial position/business, so it is still advantageous for Orsino (new money) to marry Olivia (old money) and for Malvolio and Maria to desire a marriage above their class.

context.t: Most people married in their mid to late twenties; the legal age of consent may have been as low as 12 for girls and 14 for boys.
Marrying someone of a different social standing was generally discouraged among the elite.

illyria.label: Olivia's House vs Orsino's House
illyria.note: Olivia and Orsino are both in established, great households with a steward, a set of servants, and space for their family to reside (looking at you, Toby).

keys.label: Olivia's House vs Orsino's House
keys.note: Olivia and her family are snowbirds from the Northeast, who spend their winters in the warm climate at their family-owned penthouse suite at the Hotel Illyria. Their family is well-known nationally for their philanthropy and contributions to a variety of causes in both their community and their temporary winter home. Orsino is a newer implant in the area, and is perhaps trying to exploit the tourism market. He may be building a big new home on the trendier side of town, but while he continues to live the bachelor's life, he's using the resort's amenities to pamper himself, place himself nearer to the object of his 'affection', and loosely feign management of the resort.

illyria.label: Revelry
illyria.note: Toby and company revel in the taverns of Illyria before bringing it back to Olivia's house to have wine and songs.

keys.label: Revelry
keys.note: The majority of the Fantasy Fest-esque revels happen on the main island, while on occasion small events and private entertainments will be hosted at the upscale Hotel Illyria Island Resort.

illyria.label: Twelfth Night and Fantasy Fest
illyria.note: The Lord of Misrule runs a season of Christmas revelry, in which class is collapsed for a short time to make sure everyone enjoys themselves thoroughly. The play is not really set in this season, on the Twelfth Night feast, so it acts most likely as a conceptual lens or touchpoint for Shakespeare and his audiences to grasp the chaos of the show and its characters.

keys.label: Twelfth Night and Fantasy Fest
keys.note: Similarly for our new setting, Fantasy Fest is not the direct setting of the play but the inspiration for the type of rulebending, mischief-making, and revelry we hope to depict in this production.

context.t: Fantasy Fest began in 1979 to draw tourists in the slow season.

illyria.label: The seacoast
illyria.note: Where Viola, Sebastian, and Antonio come ashore.

keys.label: The water
keys.note: The choppy waters around the Keys, where wrecks were common.
